arxiv-2207-05848.creator: Hanqing Guo 1 , Chenning Li 1 , Lingkun Li, Zhichao Cao, Qiben Yan, Li Xiao
arxiv-2207-05848.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose NEC ( N eural E nhanced C ancellation), a defense mechanism, which prevents unauthorized microphones from capturing a target speaker’s voice. arxiv-2209-01855.title: Multiple Partition Structures and Harmonic Functions on Branching Graphs
arxiv-2209-01855.creator: Eugene Strahov
arxiv-2209-01855.description: Abstract . We introduce and study multiple partition structures which are sequences of probability measures on families of Young diagrams subjected to a consistency condition. The multiple partition structures are generalizations of Kingman’s partition structures, and are motivated by a problem of population genetics.

arxiv-2303-07403.description: Abstract For glaciologists, studying ice sheets from the polar regions is critical. pmc-11309377.description: Extrapulmonary Tuberculosis (EPTB) poses challenges from patient and health system perspectives. pmc-11630482.title: The prevalence, severity, and risk factors of erosive esophagitis in a Middle Eastern population

pmc-11630482.description: Background:Erosive esophagitis (EE) is frequently present in patients with gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), some of which may not have GERD symptoms. pmc-11639816.title: Machine and Deep Learning Models for Hypoxemia Severity Triage in CBRNE Emergencies
pmc-11639816.creator: Santino Nanini, Mariem Abid, Yassir Mamouni, Arnaud Wiedemann, Philippe Jouvet, Stephane Bourassa
pmc-11639816.description: Background/Objectives: This study develops machine learning (ML) models to predict hypoxemia severity during emergency triage, particularly in Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, and Explosive (CBRNE) scenarios, using physiological data from medical-grade sensors. Methods: Tree-based models (TBMs) such as XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Random Forests (RFs), Voting Classifier ensembles, and sequential models (LSTM, GRU) were trained on the MIMIC-III and IV datasets.

pmc-11652833.title: Quantum theory of a potential biological magnetic field sensor: Radical pair mechanism in flavin adenine dinucleotide biradicals
pmc-11652833.creator: Amirhosein Sotoodehfar, Rishabh, Hadi Zadeh-Haghighi, Christoph Simon
pmc-11652833.description: Recent studies in vitro and in vivo suggest that flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD) on its own might be able to act as a biological magnetic field sensor.
